name: Protezione internazionale (refugee status and subsidiary protection)

qualifying_event.description: A well-founded fear of persecution on Convention grounds (refugee status) or a real risk of serious harm such as the death penalty, torture, or serious threat from armed conflict (subsidiary protection), per Decreto Legislativo 251/2007, implementing the EU Qualification Directive. Article 10(3) of the Italian Constitution separately guarantees a broader right of asylum to foreigners denied effective exercise of democratic freedoms in their own country.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Personal testimony plus any corroborating documentation of the persecution or risk, presented to the competent Commissione Territoriale during a formal interview.

requirement_groups.name: Refugee status or subsidiary protection determination

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a well-founded fear of persecution (refugee status) or a real risk of serious harm (subsidiary protection), assessed by one of Italy's 20 Commissioni Territoriali (with up to 30 further sub-sections) in a formal interview.
The application can be filed with border police upon entry or, at any later point, with the local Questura (police headquarters) with territorial jurisdiction over the applicant's place of residence.

evidence_required.document: Modello C3 application form, completed with interpreter assistance if needed
Passport where available, plus any documentation supporting the claim
Personal testimony at the Commissione Territoriale interview

outcome.duration_length: refugee status and subsidiary protection are granted for an unlimited period; the residence permit itself is renewed periodically (5 years for refugee status, shorter for subsidiary protection)

sources.title: Ministero dell'Interno (interno.gov.it) -- Protezione internazionale, citing DPR 21/2015 and Decreto Legislativo 251/2007, and reproducing Art. 10(3) of the Constitution
Centro di Ateneo per i Diritti Umani, Università di Padova -- Il procedimento per il riconoscimento della protezione internazionale, corroborating the application and interview procedure

notes: STRUCTURAL DETAIL, a genuinely favourable feature confirmed directly in interno.gov.it's own practical guide for applicants: while a decision is pending, if the Commissione Territoriale has not ruled within 6 months for reasons not attributable to the applicant, the residence permit is renewed for a further 6 months and the applicant gains the right to work for the remainder of the procedure -- otherwise, work rights during the pending-decision period begin 60 days after the application is filed. Italy also recognises a distinct 'protezione speciale' (special protection) category, a 2-year renewable permit granted by the Questore on the Commissione's recommendation for cases that don't meet the refugee or subsidiary-protection standard but where removal would breach other protections -- explicitly NOT convertible to a work-reason permit, a genuinely different and more limited status than full refugee/subsidiary protection, not modeled as its own separate route file here given its narrower, discretionary, non-independently-applied-for nature (the applicant cannot request it directly; only the Commissione can refer a case into it). pr_after_months and citizenship_after_months use the general 5-year/5-year figures pending confirmation of whether Italy offers refugee-status holders any accelerated naturalisation track comparable to Poland's 2-year refugee-specific tier documented elsewhere in this dataset -- this was not conclusively confirmed or ruled out in sources checked for this build and is flagged as an open question rather than asserted either way.
